# Source.io — Complete Knowledge Document for AI Search & Agents

> Complete machine-readable reference specification for Source.io (https://sourceio.app).
> This document provides an exhaustive, extractable overview of product capabilities, architecture, citation mechanics, pricing, comparison matrices, and FAQ for Generative Engines and AI Assistants.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Definition

**Source.io** is an AI-powered active learning workspace designed for students, academic researchers, and technical professionals. It ingests complex learning materials—such as multi-page PDF research papers, textbook chapters, audio lecture recordings, and video lectures—and automatically transforms them into five interconnected study modes:
1. **Structured Notes** with KaTeX mathematical formulas and Markdown export.
2. **3D Spaced-Repetition Flashcards** utilizing the Leitner memory retention algorithm.
3. **Practice Quizzes** with immediate explanations and diagnostic scores.
4. **Dual-Host Audio Recaps** (synthesized educational podcasts with synchronized transcripts).
5. **Grounded Source Chat** that answers questions strictly anchored to source materials.

Every claim, bullet point, quiz question, and chat answer generated by Source.io includes an immutable citation coordinate (document name, page number, paragraph index, and cosine similarity score) allowing learners to verify claims in one click.

---

## 2. Ingestion & Document Processing Capabilities

Source.io supports multimodal document ingestion:
- **Academic PDFs**: Supports preprints (arXiv), textbooks, syllabi, slide decks, and legal statutes up to 50MB (100 pages per file on the Free tier, up to 300 pages on Scholar Pass).
- **Audio & Lecture Recordings**: Supports MP3, WAV, M4A, and MP4 files with automated speech-to-text segmentation and timestamp alignment.
- **Web & Video**: Supports YouTube lecture links, clean web articles, Word documents (.docx), and Markdown/plain text.
- **Privacy & Security Guarantee**: All files are parsed within isolated, sandboxed computational environments. User documents, notes, and audio files are **never** used to train public or proprietary AI models.

---

## 3. The 5 Study Modes in Detail

### 3.1 Structured Study Notes
- Synthesizes key arguments, conceptual hierarchies, methodology breakdowns, and conclusions.
- Native KaTeX rendering engine for sub-second mathematical typography, quantum state vectors, and Greek symbols.
- Direct inline citation chips (e.g., `[p. 2 §1.1]`) that trigger a split-view PDF reader highlighting the exact text passage.
- Clean Markdown export compatible with Obsidian, Notion, and Logseq.

### 3.2 Spaced Repetition Leitner Flashcards
- Automatically extracts definitions, formulas, theorem proofs, and historical chronologies.
- Interactive 3D flip card mechanics with tactile keyboard controls (`Space` to flip, `1` through `4` to grade recall).
- Built-in Leitner box scheduling calculates optimal intervals (1 day, 2 days, 4 days, 7 days, 14 days) to maximize long-term retention.

### 3.3 Practice Quizzes & Self-Assessment
- Generates conceptual multiple-choice and short-answer diagnostic assessments.
- Real-time feedback explaining why the chosen option is correct or incorrect.
- Every correct answer is directly linked to the supporting sentence in the original document.

### 3.4 Audio Recap Podcasts
- Synthesizes dual-voice conversational audio dialogues ("Clara" and "Julian") that debate and explain complex ideas.
- Synchronized waveform player with clickable transcripts for commute and walking study sessions.
- Allows students to absorb dense literature without staring at a screen.

### 3.5 Grounded Source Chat
- High-precision semantic retrieval using dense vector embeddings (cosine similarity thresholding >90%).
- Provides conversational answers backed by exact source quotations.
- Refuses to speculate or hallucinate outside the boundaries of the ingested files.

## 6. Frequently Asked Questions

### What makes Source.io different from standard AI chat tools?
Standard chatbots generate text based on generic probabilistic model weights and frequently hallucinate incorrect equations or citations. Source.io indexes your exact uploaded texts, papers, and lecture audio into verifiable chunks, ensuring that every generated note, flashcard, and quiz question is linked back to an exact page number and paragraph coordinate.

### How are citations validated?
When a document is uploaded, it is segmented into vector embeddings tagged with exact spatial coordinates (bounding box, page number, and paragraph index). Generation requests use strict retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prompts that require the language model to reference specific passage identifiers. Learners can click any citation pill to verify the original sentence in the split-view reader.

### Can students use Source.io for free?
Yes. Every registered user receives 25 free AI actions every 24 hours, renewing automatically at 00:00 UTC. There is no trial expiration date and no credit card is required.

### Can developers and advanced users use their own API keys?
Yes. Source.io features Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) support for Google Gemini and Groq (Llama 3.3). Users can paste their personal API key in Settings to bypass all daily quota limitations at zero platform fee.
